title: Test and measurement
blurb: The bench: what measures a signal, what generates one, and what joins the two without melting the board.

items.s: A multimeter (also known as a multi-tester, volt-ohm-milliammeter, volt-ohmmeter or VOM, avometer or ampere-volt-ohmmeter) is a measuring instrument that can measure multiple electrical properties.

An oscilloscope (formerly known as an oscillograph, informally scope or O-scope) is a type of electronic test instrument that graphically displays varying voltages of one or more signals as a function of time.
A logic analyzer is an electronic instrument that captures and displays multiple logic signals from a digital system or digital circuit.
A spectrum analyzer measures the magnitude of an input signal versus frequency within the full frequency range of the instrument.
A network analyzer is an instrument that measures the network parameters of electrical networks.
An LCR meter is a type of electronic test equipment used to measure the inductance (L), capacitance (C), and resistance (R) of an electronic component.
The wattmeter is an instrument for measuring the electric active power (or the average of the rate of flow of electrical energy) in watts of any given circuit.
A frequency counter is an electronic instrument, or component of one, that is used for measuring frequency.
A time-domain reflectometer (TDR) is an electronic instrument used to determine the characteristics of electrical lines by observing reflected pulses.
A signal generator is one of a class of electronic devices that generates electrical signals with set properties of amplitude, frequency, and wave shape.
In electrical engineering, a function generator is usually a piece of electronic test equipment or software used to generate different types of electrical waveforms over a wide range of frequencies.
A dummy load is a device used to simulate an electrical load, usually for testing purposes.
A soldering iron is a hand tool used in soldering.

A soldering station is a multipurpose power soldering device designed for electronic components soldering.
A microscope is a laboratory instrument used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye.
A magnifying glass is a convex lens—usually mounted in a frame with a handle—that is used to produce a magnified image of an object.
An antistatic device is any device that reduces, dampens, or otherwise inhibits electrostatic discharge, or ESD, which is the buildup or discharge of static electricity.
A circuit diagram (or: wiring diagram, electrical diagram, elementary diagram, electronic schematic) is a graphical representation of an electrical circuit.

An electronic symbol is a pictogram used to represent various electrical and electronic devices or functions, such as wires, batteries, resistors, and transistors, in a schematic diagram of an electrical or electronic circuit.
A schematic, or schematic diagram, is a designed representation of the elements of a system using abstract, graphic symbols rather than realistic pictures.

An electronic color code is a system which wordlessly identifies either the functions of cables and connections, or the types and variants of electronic components.
In industrial design, preferred numbers (also called preferred values or preferred series) are standard guidelines for choosing exact product dimensions within a given set of constraints.
